messages:
Mara: Quick check 3: modal stepper vs persistent sample rail for first-run. I sketched a lightweight modal that guides users through 3 steps (API key, pick sample project, run quick test). Proto: https://figma.redwood/onboard-modal-compact
Diego: Modal pros: guided flow, higher chance to get first call. Cons: interrupts exploration. We must add a "Don't show again" option. For rail: discovery is better but could be ignored.
Priya: UX note: keep microcopy verbs-first. Examples: 'Generate API key', 'Try sample app', 'Run quick test'. For sample cards prefer 'Clone' and 'Open in Console' labels.
Owen: Dev note: prefer lazy-load modal code to avoid perf hit. Rail works as progressive enhancement (SSR-friendly). If we do modal, ensure SSR fallback is a small banner with link to docs.
A11yBot: Auto-scan summary: modal needs role="dialog", focus trap, and a visible focus indicator on close button. Contrast check: progress dot color fails 3:1. Recommendation: use high-contrast stroke and text alternatives for progress ("Step 2 of 3").
Lena: Analytics: track path (modal_open, modal_complete, rail_interact, sample_clone, api_key_create). Also save onboarding choice in backend cookie so we don't show modal repeatedly.
Mara: Decision: prototype rail-first (smaller perf impact, better discovery). But build a lightweight modal as a fallback guided path for new users who opt-in. Action items: Diego build rail proto with sticky behavior; Owen add inert handling for mount focus; Priya copy pass; A11yBot + Lena run checks. Target: staging demo Thursday.
Diego: Will do sticky rail with keyboard test and lazy images. ETA Wed PR.
Owen: I'll add inert/polyfill snippet and SSR banner fallback.
Priya: I'll update copy and add microtooltips for API key safety.
A11yBot: I'll re-run axe on PR and post report link.
Mara: Thanks all 3 tagging reviewers for PR once ready.
